So... are your controllers compromised? Would you even know?
Configs are rarely checked against a golden baseline.

text.headline: Configs are rarely checked against a *golden baseline.*
text.status: last compared to golden config: NEVER

scenes.vo: Every vendor has its own proprietary software. It costs thousands per seat, and none of it was built for cybersecurity.

text.headline: Every vendor, *its own proprietary software.*
text.securitySub: designed for engineering, one device at a time

scenes.vo: What if one tool could see them all?
Meet PEAT. The Process Extraction and Analysis Tool, from Sandia National Laboratories.
Scan finds and fingerprints O-T devices.

text.title: Find & *fingerprint* OT devices
text.sub: Discovers what's on the network and verifies vendor and model.

scenes.vo: Pull grabs logic, configs, logs, and firmware, over Ethernet or serial.

text.title: Collect the *artifacts* that matter
text.sub: Deep, read-focused collection from live devices.

scenes.vo: Parse turns proprietary blobs into one data model.

text.title: One *data model.* Every vendor.
text.sub: Proprietary formats decoded into standardized, human-readable JSON.

scenes.vo: Then diff it against your golden config, or stream it into Elastic or Splunk.

text.title: Catch *every change*
text.sub: Compare against your golden config, then send results to your SIEM.

scenes.vo: And it's built for sensitive, live controllers. PEAT verifies each device before it pulls, fingerprints them one at a time, and only collects what you ask for.

text.headline: Built for *live, sensitive* controllers
items: Fingerprints one device at a time
Collects only what you ask for

scenes.vo: Out of the box, PEAT collects from PLCs, protection relays, RTUs, and more, across over ten vendors.

scenes.vo: PEAT itself runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, or Docker, and it's easy to download and start using.
Prefer code? Import PEAT as a Python library, and build it into your own tools.

text.title: Use it as a *Python library*
text.sub: Script pulls, parsing and analysis into your own tools.
